title: Ceiling Painting & Popcorn Removal | Gainesville FL
description: Popcorn ceiling removal, skim coating, and flat ceiling painting in Gainesville, Ocala, and North Central Florida. Testing first, smooth finish after.
h1: Ceiling Painting and Popcorn Ceiling Removal in North Central Florida
heroIntro: We take dated textured ceilings down to the board, skim them flat, and finish with a clean flat paint. We also repaint existing smooth and knockdown ceilings that are stained, yellowed, or patchy.
card: Popcorn texture removed, ceilings skimmed smooth or knockdown, and finished with a uniform flat paint.

questions: Do I need to test my popcorn ceiling for asbestos before removing it?
Should I go smooth or knockdown after popcorn removal?
Can you just paint over a popcorn ceiling?

body: Sprayed acoustic texture was a fast, cheap way to hide drywall seams for decades. Today it reads as dated, it traps dust and cooking film, and it is almost impossible to patch invisibly after a roof leak or a light fixture move. Popcorn ceiling removal is one of the biggest visual upgrades you can make to a room, especially before listing a home or after a kitchen remodel.

This page covers the full ceiling service: removal, repair, skim coating, texture choice, and paint. If your main concern is keeping dust out of an occupied home, read about our dustless popcorn removal method, which uses vacuum extraction and sealed containment.

We see the most requests from owners of 1970s and 1980s ranch homes, investors preparing rentals between tenants, and families who just bought a house and want the ceilings done before furniture arrives. An empty house is the easiest time to do it, but occupied homes are routine too. Ceiling work is one of several specialty services we schedule alongside standard painting.

sections.h2: Test older texture before anyone scrapes it
body: Some acoustic ceiling textures applied before the mid-1980s contained asbestos. You cannot tell by looking. Before an older ceiling is disturbed, a sample should be lab-tested. If the result is positive, the texture must be handled by a licensed abatement contractor, not a painting crew, and we will tell you so plainly rather than proceed.
Our blog post on popcorn ceilings and asbestos walks through what testing involves and what your options are. Once a ceiling is cleared, we schedule the removal.

sections.h2: How the removal and refinish works
body: Rooms are emptied or furniture is moved to the center and wrapped. Floors and walls are masked floor to ceiling, and HVAC vents and fixtures are covered. The texture is misted so it softens and releases in sheets, then scraped down to the drywall.

Removal is only half the job. Scraping exposes tape joints, gouges, and fasteners that the texture was hiding, so crews tape, fill, and skim coat the ceiling until it reads flat under a raking light. Painting over an uneven skim only makes the flaws easier to see.
bullets: Lab test confirmed clear on older ceilings before work begins
Full masking of floors, walls, vents, and fixtures
Wet scraping to the board, then joint and fastener repair
Skim coat sanded smooth, or a light knockdown if you prefer
Stain-blocking primer and a sprayed flat ceiling finish

sections.h2: Smooth, knockdown, or a fresh coat on an existing ceiling
body: A smooth ceiling looks clean and modern but demands the most skim work, because every ripple shows. A light knockdown texture is more forgiving on older homes where the framing is not perfectly flat. We will show you both on the walkthrough and recommend the one your ceiling can support.

Not every ceiling needs removal. Smooth and knockdown ceilings that are yellowed, water-stained, or patched in a different white simply need repainting. Water stains are sealed with a stain-blocking primer first so they do not bleed back through. If there is sagging or soft drywall from a leak, our drywall repair and patching crew replaces the damaged section before the ceiling is painted.

sections.h2: Finish products, sequencing, and living at home during the work
body: Ceilings are painted with a dead-flat ceiling paint because any sheen exaggerates the shadows of a skimmed surface, especially in rooms with long windows or recessed lights. Kitchens and baths may get a washable flat or matte product that tolerates steam and cooking film. Where you want a low-odor option for bedrooms or a nursery, low-VOC lines from Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore are available, and the product is named on the estimate.

Ceiling work also has its own sequencing. Removal, repair, and skim coating happen first and need drying time before sanding and primer. A room typically moves from scraping to finished paint over several days because joint compound has to dry in our humid air before it can be sanded cleanly. Rushing that step is how ceilings end up with flashing and visible seams.

You do not need to move out. Crews work room by room and protect furniture as they go. A single ceiling is often wrapped into the same visit as wall painting, which makes sense because removal and sanding scuff the upper walls anyway. Pairing the ceiling with interior wall painting means one round of masking and one cleanup. Your written estimate lists every ceiling included, the finish chosen, products, and the schedule.

faqs.q: Can you just paint over a popcorn ceiling?
faqs.a: You can, but paint makes the texture harder to remove later and tends to pull loose patches off with the roller. If the texture is sound and you plan to keep it, we can spray it. Most people asking are better served by removal.
Older texture should be sampled and lab-tested before it is disturbed. If it tests positive, it needs a licensed abatement contractor. We do not scrape texture that has not been cleared.

faqs.q: Will the ceiling look perfectly flat afterward?
faqs.a: We skim and sand until the ceiling reads flat under a raking light. On framing that is out of plane, we may recommend a light knockdown instead of a smooth finish so the result looks even.

faqs.q: Do I need to leave the house?
faqs.a: No. Crews work room by room and protect furniture. If you have allergy concerns or cannot clear rooms, ask about our dustless removal method.
